name: Turtle
canonicalMarkers: domed shell covering the whole trunk
head and neck poking out the front
canonicalNote: Generic name interpreted as a representative freshwater pond turtle. Commonly drawn with the shell as a separate hat sitting on the back; the shell IS the body wall, legs and neck emerge from under its rim.

sourceCoverage.declarations: External pinnae are anatomically absent (chelonian). Four visible feet, exposed neck, head and tail are hand-authored on the exact original.
sourceCoverage.limitations: Interior root/spine/pelvis/chest points are source-local control frames inside the shell, not seen bones. Far limb emergence under the shell is partly occluded; far hip/shoulder landmarks are interpretations under the shell rim. Each ankle part is the whole visible foot block with the ankle landmark in its interior (the C266 tortoise a02/a03 lesson).

ownerCheckEvidence: Exact input copies match existing independently controlled owner-check inputs; sourceOwnerCheck is retained existing result, not a new run.
